items.item: Compare each genre’s two briefs as the engine reads them: dramatic circumstances, objectives and obstacles, technique demands, preparation actions, valid interpretations, feedback and consequences
items.requirement: Brief 09 section 3: “Matching preferences alone do not prove identical gameplay. Compare their actual …”; genres.md item 1: as the engine reads them, not their wording.
items.currentBehavior: No tool compares a genre’s two briefs in what the engine reads. tests/briefs-content.test.ts “two situations for every genre” holds their wording apart and two of eight setting axes different; tests/briefs-situations.test.ts holds four actors’ results apart by 0.5; neither reads the readings, the preparation or what the take names.
items.plan: A read-only tool reading each genre’s two briefs through the engine’s own functions (briefMaterial, sceneOf, suitabilityOf, briefContext, judgePiece, taskOf, rehearseTrains, rehearseSpeed, stepMinutes, turnsOf, heartOf, chiefLimit) in six parts, each “the same” by a rule written here before any brief changed: circumstances (medium and language the same, stakes within one); objectives and obstacles (the reader’s behavior the same, and the changes of tone plus beats held two ways within one); technique demands (the same task, the same techniques, the five features within 2 in all); preparation (the same length, what rehearsal trains and what speeds it); valid interpretations (two or more readings of one matching a reading of the other in the dimension it leans most and the ability it draws most); feedback and consequences (the specialist rewarded most and the dimension the half-prepared take names as its limit). Substantively repetitive: the same in three of the six or more (half of what the engine reads). Measured with the rule before any change: 14 of the 55 (0 same: 7, 1: 15, 2: 19, 3: 9, 4: 3, 5: 2).
items.acceptance: tools/genre-pairs.ts output before and after; tests/remaining-genres.test.ts holds the rule’s verdict on the 55.
